text: Fit the two lower-frequency spectral branches' amplitude-vs-temperature decay to the expected thermal-damping form.
Lighter branch effective mass = 0.039 +- 0.002 electron masses.
Lighter branch per-window fits scattered between 0.032 and 0.049 electron masses.
Heavier branch effective mass = 0.048 +- 0.003 electron masses.
Heavier branch per-window fits were stable at 0.048-0.049 electron masses across field windows.
The mass fitted for the combined (sum-frequency) tone (0.051-0.069) is heavier than the heavy branch.
In the upper field window, the sum-tone mass approaches the sum of the light and heavy branch masses.
Because the sum-tone mass is heavier than the light branch alone, a simple 'beat' interpretation (two closely spaced frequencies from a single pocket) was excluded.
This exclusion is read as a decisive indicator of two genuinely distinct Fermi pockets plus a combination orbit, rather than a separate third pocket.

A faint, gate-voltage-only feature (not displacement-field-dependent) appears in the 2D map at a fixed value of the fast-axis gate, present across every slow-axis value, located away from the density corridor of interest.
Interpreted as a spatially localized region of the device gated by only one of the two gates (e.g., an arm not covered by one gate layer), rather than a bulk electronic feature.
Flagged as a device-inhomogeneity note without further investigation this session.
Designed a coarse 2D gate map across the full accessible gate box (back gate slow axis, top gate fast axis at finer resolution) to trace the displacement-field dependence of the resistance peak.
Reasoning: an exponential rise with |D| would indicate one candidate stacking order.
Reasoning: a modest field-symmetric rise would indicate a second candidate stacking order.
Reasoning: a field-asymmetric rise would indicate a third candidate stacking order.
This map was designed as the session's first stacking-order discriminator.
On the opposite-carrier-sign spot check, oscillation onset occurs at a somewhat higher field than the first side.
A dominant low frequency and a weaker higher frequency (~38% of the dominant peak's amplitude) are found.

The higher frequency scales with density between the two sides consistent with a real Fermi surface tracking the expected area-density relation (density ratio matches frequency ratio to within a few percent).
The lower frequency survives and dominates on this side, where the bound-pair model predicts it should nearly vanish.
Confirmed the lower frequency is not a harmonic of the higher frequency (no longer an exact half/double relationship once measured independently on this side).
Both findings actively strain, rather than resolve, the three-way structural fork carried from the first spot check.
The fainter, more lightly doped secondary region (probed only in series with the dominant region through the same voltage-probe pair) was judged uninformative on its own for the stacking call.
Reason: no tone set attributable solely to it was resolved.
Its predicted tones (shifted to somewhat higher frequency than the dominant region's) were judged to fall within the frequency resolution of the dominant region's tones, at low relative weight.
Final call for the one measured contact pair: Bernal (ABAB) stacking, stated as a strong determination.
Based on a saturating, meV-scale, field-symmetric neutrality-point gap.
Based on a four-fold degenerate Landau-level sequence with zero-state crossings at zero displacement field.
Based on a displacement-field-split two-fold sequence with a monotonic zero-state at finite displacement field.
Based on the temperature-activation results.
All evaluated on the session's own in-session density and displacement-field calibration.
No other region of the device was measurable this session, since every other spare contact pair was dead or unconnected as provided.
The call is explicitly scoped to the single measured region.
Campaign call upgraded from 'strong' to 'strong, two-branch' for the same channel and stacking-order assignment.
Both the originally-called branch and the newly resolved light branch are now treated as directly observed evidence for the same order.
This retires the earlier hedge that the light pocket was unresolved.
The competing single-rescaled-surface reading is now stated to be fully dissolved under the revised scale.
Attributed to the light branch having been unresolved at the time, rather than to a genuine single-surface degeneracy.
Remaining softness: the light branch's own effective mass is still unmeasured.
Remaining softness: the absolute density-scale calibration is still pending an independent cross-check.
Judged the device alive on the wired current path from the four single-gate liveness legs.
Drain current stayed at 9.8-9.97 nA (full bias reaching the drain) on every leg.
Pickup channel read 60-320 ohms, smooth and structured, on all four legs.
The contact pair was judged alive and ohmic over a full top-gate sweep at zero back-gate voltage.
Longitudinal resistance ran only about 40-370 ohm with no charge-neutrality peak in that cut.
The monotonic resistance trend was read as the device being electron-doped at zero back-gate voltage.
The neutrality point was inferred to lie outside the swept top-gate window.
Committed to an approximately eight-hour, six-rung temperature ladder at the fixed electron-side gate point (ascending nominal setpoints, alternating field-sweep direction each rung).
Included automatic stability and thermal-runaway guards, with heaters forced off on any early exit.
Chose to proceed without a confirmed remaining-cryogen figure from the operator, after asking for it and not receiving an answer.
Relied on the standing autonomy grant and the operator's ability to halt any individual rung.
Ramping the silicon gate from zero toward one polarity of its card limit does not open the source-drain contact.
Drain current stays pinned near its zero-gate baseline (~88 pA) across the entire sweep.
Designed and ran a second SdH spot check on the hole side, at the most negative density reachable on the D=0 line within the gate limits (about -1.2e12 cm^-2).
Rode the magnet down from 10 T to 0.3 T at 20 mT steps (486 points), sensitivity 50 microV.
Explicitly framed as a cheap, non-decisive preview rather than a decisive test.
Reason: a null result there would be resolution- and mass-limited rather than genuine evidence against the alternative stacking.
Final campaign call for the device's wired voltage-probe pair (probing the two series-connected doping regions together): the stacking is ABAB (Bernal), rated 'strong.'
Based on the closing Luttinger frequency sum.
Based on both SdH branches tracking the ABAB model's density dependence across the fan.
Based on the combination-tone origin of the summed frequency.
Based on the Lifshitz-Kosevich mass split (light mass matching the model exactly, with a decisive beat exclusion).
Hedge: the heavy-branch mass remains an unresolved extraction-window fork.
Hedge: only a single voltage-probe pair was available, so a different stacking confined to the weakly-doped secondary region cannot be excluded.
Measured heavy-to-light mass ratio (about 1.2-1.4) falls well short of the favored stacking model's predicted ratio (~2.2) at this density.
Flagged explicitly as not matching the model's specific mass-ratio prediction.
Treated as a hedge on the stacking call rather than evidence for a different stacking order.
Reason: the lighter branch's mass rests on a short, low-resolution frequency record, called the softest number in the analysis.
Reason: no competing model was judged able to reproduce the full observed pattern of frequencies, partition, and masses together.
Interpreted the two lower oscillation frequencies as fundamentals of two distinct Fermi-surface pockets.
Their sum (6.2+21.8=28.0 T) matches the observed higher-frequency peak (28.1 T).
Their difference (21.8-6.2=15.6 T) matches the observed lowest-frequency peak (15.6 T).
This sum-and-difference intermodulation set is read as consistent with inter-pocket magnetic breakdown, rather than an artifact of two separate, non-interacting current paths.
Charge-neutrality-point resistance grows substantially with displacement field along the fitted ridge, roughly doubling from the field-symmetric point to the most extreme field sampled on the map.
This pattern is flagged as consistent with a displacement-field-tunable gap of the kind expected for one specific stacking order.
Explicitly noted the achieved electron temperature is too high for this alone to diagnose a gap.
The observation is carried forward only as a supporting/domain caveat, referenced again after the electron-side spot check and in the final call's hedge list.
Using the density calibration from the first field-ramp sweep with no free parameters, the second sweep's roughly 204 resistance minima fell in steps of two rather than four.
This is read as the displacement field lifting a two-fold degeneracy of the Landau levels.
The zero-filling-factor state grew monotonically with field, with no crossings.
This is consistent with the field having polarized the zero-energy manifold, rather than leaving it in the crossing regime seen at zero displacement field.

The physical zero of displacement field was located from the symmetry vertex of the dominant ridge's resistance minimum plotted against raw displacement field (vertex at roughly +0.012-0.013 V/nm raw).
This offset was adopted as the D=0 reference for all subsequent gate-voltage-to-(n,D) conversions.
Designed a temperature ladder from base temperature up to 50 K, at five displacement-field points spanning the reference point and both gapped and near-neutral settings identified by the fine map.

Purpose: to measure the thermal activation of the field-induced gap and settle whether it matches the meV scale expected for one candidate stacking order or the much larger scale expected for another.
Purpose: separately, to determine whether the zero-field plateau's resistance is thermally activated (a real gap) or temperature-independent (a residual/parallel conduction path).
Launched the first zero-field 2D gate map, sweeping one gate over its full card-limit range on the fast axis.
Swept the other gate over a reduced window (about half its card-limit range) on the slow axis.
This traded full coverage of the second gate (which would add roughly three more hours) for keeping the neutrality line inside the fast-axis window over the density range the campaign actually needs.
Because the neutrality point was not found in the top-gate cut, chose to sweep the back gate next (at zero top-gate voltage) rather than go straight to a full 2D map.
Reasoning: a geometry-based lever-arm estimate indicated the back gate reaches further into the hole side.
This made it the cheaper way to locate the neutrality point.
Delivered the campaign's final stacking determination for the measured contact pair as one particular stacking order.
Stated strength: 'strong, not decisive.'
Chose to sweep the silicon gate through zero to the opposite polarity's card limit.
Reasoning: if the contact metal dopes the leads one way, the opposite gate polarity might open them where the first polarity did not.
The sweep overlaps the first leg's range as an in-situ hysteresis check.
Designed and ran a Lifshitz-Kosevich mass-ladder measurement at the same electron-side spot (density +3.2e12 cm^-2, D=0).
Six temperature rungs: base ~1.2 K plus 6, 10, 15, 22, and 30 K, set via the heater's authorized dual-loop method with a hover-acceptance criterion.
Field swept back and forth over a fixed 2-7 T window at 25 mT per rung, sensitivity 50 microV.
Priced at about 5 h 10 m.
Decided the mass fits would rely on the heated rungs and treat the base-temperature point only as a free cross-check rather than a fit input.
Reasoning: the rig's nominal base electron temperature (per the rig card) is expected to exceed the thermometer reading.
A third tracked tone equals the sum of the light and heavy branch frequencies at essentially every fan column.
This total matches the expected fourfold-degenerate frequency across the whole density range.
A fourth, nearly density-independent tone equals the difference of the light and heavy branch frequencies at every column.

The flat, non-Onsager trajectory of this difference tone was read as establishing that the sum tone is a combination/intermodulation orbit of the two real Fermi pockets, allowed by symmetry under ABAB stacking.
Rather than a separate pocket belonging to an alternative (ABCA) stacking domain.
Designed and launched a contact-doping sweep on the silicon back gate, ramping from zero to the card limit.
Both other gates held at zero during the sweep.
Watched the drain current for any recovery toward the drive target.
Sum-frequency tone's mass exceeds both fundamental masses.
Sum-frequency tone's mass increases between field windows.
This is read as consistent with an additive magnetic-breakdown-orbit mass (an orbit traversing both underlying pockets), rather than a single Fermi pocket of fixed mass.
Committed to a full 2D gate map spanning the whole validator box: 66 fast-axis points at 20 mV steps by 67 slow-axis points at 50 mV steps.
Fixed the pickup sensitivity so that only the highest-resistance corners of the map would be allowed to saturate.
Designed and ran a Landau fan on the electron side at D=0: density swept from about 1.60 to 3.25e12 cm^-2 (61 points).
At each of 101 field rows spaced uniformly in 1/B from 1 to 10 T.
Sensitivity fixed at 100 microV, fast-axis delay 1.2 s.
Priced at about 3 h 55 m.
The lower field bound (1.0 T) and lower density bound (~1.6e12) were both set from the electron-side spot check's observed tone-onset behavior.
Concluded the lighter of the two fundamental branches is measurably lighter than the heavier one, about 2.4 standard deviations apart.
Took this as ruling out the possibility that the lighter branch is merely a beat pattern of the heavier tone.
Concluded instead it is an independent, genuine second electronic band.
On operator direction to improve the data for a publication-quality figure, redesigned essentially the same density-versus-field map on the same carrier-sign side.
Used a roughly 3x longer lock-in time constant on all channels.
Extended the field window down below the previously measured oscillation onset, because that sub-onset region is where the candidate light pocket's oscillations should be visible.
Roughly doubled the number of field rows for finer per-column frequency resolution.
This redesigned map cost roughly 2.5x the wall-clock cost of the original map.
Tracking two SdH branches column-by-column across the fan's 61 densities shows both following the ABAB-stacking model's predicted frequency-vs-density curves under the single 0.886 density scale.
Light branch spans roughly 3.0-7.5 T against a model curve of 1.8-6.3 T.
Heavy branch spans roughly 13.9-22.1 T against a model curve of 13-22.9 T.
An alternative trilayer (monolayer+bilayer) stacking model was excluded because its predicted partner-branch trajectory (near 1-2 T) did not match either observed branch.
The drain current passes a stable ~92 pA through the device at zero gate voltages.
This current is completely unmodulated by sweeping either gate to the card limits.
The ~109 MOhm source-drain resistance is judged to sit outside the gated channel (in the silicon-gated lead/contact regions).
Four-terminal liveness is called partial/unresolved rather than failed.
The zero-filling-factor state's resistance grew with field but non-monotonically.
It dipped rather than rose in two field windows: ~2.2-2.5 T and ~6.7-7.3 T.
These dips were read as Landau-level crossings within the zero-energy manifold characteristic of the favored candidate stacking order.
This contrasts with the alternative candidate's expectation of monotonic growth.
Designed and launched a mirror-density spot check on the opposite carrier-sign side of the neutrality point.
Rode the field back down from the first check's endpoint, rather than re-traversing back through zero field.
Inherited the same field grid and lock-in sensitivities as the first check, for a same-scale comparison.
Chose an electron-side operating point at a target density of about +3.0x10^12 cm^-2 at zero displacement field.
Field sweep from 0 to 10 T at uniform field steps (417 points).
Pickup channel left in autorange rather than fixed.
Elected to leave the magnet parked at 10 T afterward rather than ramp back down.
The wired voltage-probe pair's raw resistance drops sharply, from about 52 to 12 ohms, within the first 0.5 T of field.
Interpreted as a Hall-voltage (rho_xy) admixture from the pair straddling a corner of the flake, rather than being a clean longitudinal probe pair.
Judged harmless for extracting SdH oscillation frequencies.
But relevant to any quantitative use of the raw resistance as rho_xx.
A roughly 1% admixture of the transverse (Hall) resistance into the longitudinal signal was present throughout the session, because only one magnetic-field polarity was measured.
This admixture was judged to distort harmonic frequency content.
But not the position of the fundamental frequency components or the sum-partition used for the stacking call.
Therefore no part of the final call rests on harmonic-frequency features.
Designed the oscillation spot-check sweep at five fixed density points along the measured zero-displacement-field line.
Four points on the electron side spanning toward the discrimination window.
One point on the hole side, deliberately included despite being known to fall in the models' non-discriminating range.
Sampled on a single field traverse at a resolution set by three times the Nyquist rate of the expected highest oscillation frequency.
Final stacking-order call for the only wired four-terminal region: rhombohedral-type, at moderate (not strong) confidence.
Based on a 10.4x displacement-field-driven gap at neutrality.
Based on a gap minimum centered on zero displacement field.
Based on a displacement-field-driven metal-to-insulator crossover at neutrality.
Based on a single Fermi pocket.
For the Landau fan, swept field from 0.75 T up to a 6 T ceiling, well under the session's field cap, upward once without retracing.
Density axis co-swept along the just-measured charge-neutrality line from n = -1.04e12 to +2.10e12 cm^-2.
This range was centered on neutrality so both carrier signs were covered.
While the Landau fan was running, the neutrality-column resistance was climbing fast enough to be about to exceed the lock-in's range.
Chose not to re-range the sensitivity.
Judgment: the loss of the neutrality column's magnitude was cheaper than losing the finite-density quantum-oscillation minima the current sensitivity was tuned for.
The true charge-neutrality point was found to sit between the two zero-field resistance ridges, at a local resistance minimum.
Flanked by the two ridges as maxima.
This shape is consistent with (but not diagnostic of) a semimetal with overlapping electron and hole pockets, which the campaign's target stacking order is predicted to be.
Logged explicitly as a consistent-with observation rather than evidence for stacking.
Inferred that two-terminal contact resistance, not the channel, dominates the drain-current dip seen near neutrality.
Estimated roughly 0.4 MOhm of resistance per contact.
This contact resistance roughly doubles through the neutrality point.

Claimed a rhombohedral four-layer stack's Landau-level degeneracy (single 16-fold-degenerate zero-energy level, giving first flanking gaps at filling factor +/-8) would look visibly different from a Bernal-stacked four-layer's Landau-level sequence.
Claimed that counting filling factors alone would settle the stacking order.
Noted the down-sweep's pocket-count result cannot exclude a small second Fermi pocket carrying under roughly ten per cent of the carriers.
Reason: a tone from such a pocket would fall at a low frequency (below ~1.5 T) that the polynomial background-removal step used before the spectral fit would remove along with the background.

Across the higher-resolution sweep's full density range, the observed partner-component fraction tracked the primary candidate stacking model's predicted trend (rising with density) far more closely than the alternative fewer-layer model.
The average deviation from the primary model was about seven-fold smaller than the deviation from the alternative.
Judged a decisive discrimination between the two models.
Final campaign-goal call for the measured channel: a strong determination of the primary candidate stacking order.
The frequency component at the reference frequency identified specifically as a symmetry-allowed inter-block composite (breakdown) orbit, rather than a signature of the alternative stacking order.
The call was stated to be limited to the one measurable region.
And to the electron carrier side only.
Chose to take the density-scale lever arm from the second calibration sweep.
Chose to take the charge-neutrality location from the first sweep, rather than averaging the two sweeps' results.
Reason: the second sweep's ray slopes were robust (6% scatter) while its ray intercepts converged poorly (only 3 of 7 within tolerance, versus much tighter convergence in the first sweep).
Corrected its own summary: the n=+1.99x10^12 cm^-2 trace actually returned no unflagged tone at all (all candidates flagged marginal or harmonic).
Therefore the true result is four of five densities gave a single clean tone, not all five.
Recognized the activation gap is visibly curved (parabolic) near its minimum rather than linear.
Fit a parabola to the ~29 points around the minimum.
Located the gap's zero-crossing displacement field at D = +0.016 +/- 0.004 V/nm.
Chose to move directly to a field-based (Landau-level) calibration approach, rather than attempting a further zero-field analysis to identify the charge-neutrality line.
Reasoning: only the exact Landau degeneracy relation could fix the absolute density scale and unambiguously identify the charge-neutrality point without relying on any assumed capacitance ratio.
Set the campaign's measurement order as a coarse gate map first, as the cheapest stacking discriminator.
Then a Landau fan as an independent band-structure/pocket-count check.
With the temperature ladder run last, because the cooldown after it is passive and slow.
From the Landau fan's minima, found a uniform filling-factor spacing consistent with the standard four-fold spin-valley degeneracy.
Adopted that degeneracy over two-fold or eight-fold alternatives.
Reason: it gives the most physically plausible top-gate dielectric thickness (11.1 nm vs. ~9.5 nm stated for the stack), versus ~22 nm (two-fold, implausible) and ~5.5 nm (eight-fold, unlikely).
Noted this assumption is not needed for the stacking call itself.
A test for whether the dominant frequency component is a field-dependent composite (breakdown) orbit rather than an independent oscillation was completed decisively on the higher-resolution sweep.
Compared the component's amplitude in the low- versus high-field half of the record, now at equal frequency resolution in both halves.
10 of 13 testable density columns behaved as expected for a composite orbit.
Zero columns behaved like an independent oscillation (3 inconclusive).
The amplitude ratio between halves grew by roughly five- to thirty-fold.
